progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Fresh Year 12 students have met reproduction and DNA as inherited information in B1. This lesson reminds them that sperm and egg are reproductive cells called gametes. No meiosis, chromosome sets or haploid terminology is assumed.
progression.startsWith: Two named examples have eggs outside the body. Ask where sperm and egg actually joined.
progression.stopsAfter: Classify fertilisation by joining location and explain how water, proximity, timing and current affect opportunities for gametes to meet in a stated comparison. Do not infer exact fertilisation or offspring counts.
progression.nextLesson: bio-m5-b02b delivery part 1: How does a flower make a seed? Detailed mammalian reproduction follows later.

teaching.task: Locate sperm-and-egg joining in named animal examples and explain how supplied conditions affect encounters; distinguish joining inside from later egg laying outside.
teaching.causalExplanation: A sperm must reach an egg before joining. Nearby release reduces distance; water limits drying and lets sperm swim. A current can increase separation. In the hen, the moist internal tract reduces drying, and joining precedes shell formation and laying.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Follow two familiar organisms with plain subject-action sentences. Introduce gametes and oviduct with short meanings. After explaining the hen sequence, use join, shell, lay as a hen-specific memory anchor.
teaching.openingDecision: Compare eggs in pond water and a nest to challenge classification from final egg location. A separate generic misconception scene is unnecessary because the hen sequence resolves this precise misconception.
teaching.understandingCheck: Two groups have equal gamete numbers, release time and viable lifetime. A stronger current carries sperm away in B. Students classify, predict meeting opportunities with a cause, and name an unknown count. Prompt, provisional 12-second quiet hold and separate feedback must be reassembled from measured narration.
teaching.curriculumScope: Focused bio-m5-b02a route: animal external/internal fertilisation in common frog and hen, causal conditions and application. This candidate does not establish complete dotpoint or practical coverage.
